question: Ashish’s salary is ₹11,000 per month. He spends ₹4,000 on house rent and ₹1,500 on bills, and the rest of the amount is his monthly savings. Find his savings (in ₹) in a year, if in the month of his birthday, he spent all his monthly savings on birthday celebrations.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Monthly Savings** = 11,000 − (4,000 + 1,500) = ₹5,500.

Total months in a year = 12.

Birthday month savings spent = 1 month.

**Total Savings in a year** = 5,500 × (12 − 1) = 5,500 × 11 = ₹60,500.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹60,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c6ee407e40f2e29534d3e3d42f74507075f6dff5f1950877016c5e0179b2e1f.png] 

**Given:**

Monthly salary = ₹11,000

Expenditure on Rent = ₹4,000

Expenditure on Bills = ₹1,500

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total monthly expenditure = 4,000 + 1,500 = ₹5,500

⇒ Monthly savings = 11,000 − 5,500 = ₹5,500

⇒ Annual savings (without birthday expense) = 5,500 × 12 = ₹66,000

⇒ Amount spent on birthday = Monthly savings of 1 month = ₹5,500

⇒ Final annual savings = 66,000 − 5,500 = ₹60,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹60,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure and Savings

The basic relationship is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any change in two variables affects the third proportionally.

Percentage Savings

Savings % = (Savings ÷ Total Income) × 100. This is useful for comparing financial habits across different income levels.

Annualization

To convert monthly figures to annual, multiply by 12. If a specific one-time expense occurs, subtract it from the total annual calculation.
